sections.title: The Final Vision of the New Jerusalem
observations: In this section, John describes the river of the water of life, clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb. This imagery symbolizes the eternal life and sustenance that God provides to His people in the new creation.

The tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit, represents the abundance and variety of blessings that will be available to the redeemed. Its leaves are for the healing of the nations, indicating that there will be no more curse or suffering in this new reality.

sections.title: The Eternal State of the Redeemed
observations: John emphasizes that God's servants will serve Him and reign forever. This highlights the intimate relationship between God and His people, as well as the fulfillment of the promise that believers will reign with Christ.
The absence of night and the presence of God's glory signify the complete removal of sin and darkness, allowing for unbroken fellowship with God.

sections.title: The Assurance of Christ's Return
observations: Jesus declares, 'I am coming soon,' which serves as both a promise and a call to readiness for believers. This statement underscores the imminent return of Christ and the urgency of living in light of that return.
The response of the church, 'Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!' reflects the longing of believers for Christ's return and the establishment of His kingdom.

sections.title: The Warning Against Adding or Taking Away from the Prophecy
observations: John concludes the book with a stern warning about altering the words of the prophecy. This emphasizes the importance of adhering to the truth of Scripture and the seriousness of God's revelation.
The promise of judgment for those who alter the text serves as a reminder of the sanctity of God's Word and the consequences of disobedience.

importantVerses.commentary: The river of the water of life symbolizes the eternal sustenance provided by God.
Jesus' promise of His imminent return encourages believers to remain vigilant and faithful.
The warning against altering the prophecy highlights the importance of preserving the integrity of God's Word.

questions: What does the imagery of the river of life and the tree of life teach us about God's provision in the new creation?
How should the promise of Christ's imminent return affect our daily lives and priorities as believers?
What are the implications of the warning against adding to or taking away from the prophecy for our understanding of Scripture?
